From your shelf, **Sushi Go!** is the best fit for portable + versatile at **2–5**.

**Portability:** Small box, just cards, no board. Toss it in a bag and you are done.

**Versatility at 2–5:** It actually works at every count in that range. Two-player is tight; five-player stays fast because turns are simultaneous. Kids, non-gamers, and hobby friends all get it. Teach is basically “pick a card, pass the hand.”

| **Rainbow** | Yes — tiny box | Yes (2–6) | Less “everyone gets it” than Sushi Go |
| **Las Vegas** | Meh — dice + casino boards | Yes | Fun, but bulkier than a card game |

_**Agent (auto-low)**_

From your shelf, here is the **five-game travel bag** I would pack — all small, all table-friendly, and each covers a different mood so you are not bringing five versions of the same game.

### The five

1. **Sushi Go!** — Your default. **2–5**, cards only, teaches in two minutes, simultaneous so nobody stalls. The game you pull out when you do not know who is showing up.

2. **Monopoly Deal** — Second deck, different vibe. **2–5**, pure cards, familiar name, finishes in ~15 minutes. Take-that and rent-charging when the table wants a little bite. The Monopoly you can actually complete.

3. **Rainbow** — Smallest box in the bag. **2–6**, quick rounds, combo tricks and prize cards. Fills the "we want something sharp and done in twenty minutes" slot without another drafting game.

4. **Point Salad** — The thinkier card game. **2–6**, still just cards, but everyone builds their own scoring engine. Good when the group is past gateway mode but you still want portability.

5. **Fluxx** — The chaos pick. **2–6**, one deck, rules change on the table. Pull it when people want silly, not strategic — and when nobody minds that the plan lasts about thirty seconds.

### What this bag covers

| Need | Game |
|------|------|
| Any count 2–5+ | Sushi Go!, Monopoly Deal, Rainbow, Point Salad, Fluxx |
| Fastest teach | Sushi Go! |
| Familiar name for skeptics | Monopoly Deal |
| Smallest footprint | Rainbow |
| Most depth in a card box | Point Salad |
| Party energy | Fluxx |

### What I would not pack (even though you own them)

- **Jaipur, Hanamikoji, Agent Avenue, Santorini** — excellent, but **two-player only**. Pack one if you travel as a pair; skip for a general 2–5 bag.
- **Las Vegas** — great game, but dice + casino boards are bulkier than a pure card game.
- **Dixit** — big box, big cards, needs table space; better for home game night.
- **Deception** — needs **4+** and a group that wants a murder mystery.
- **Catan: On the Road** — portable, but **3–4 only** and overlaps with Monopoly Deal as the "familiar franchise" slot.

### Swaps if your table looks different

- **Often just two of you?** Swap **Fluxx** for **Jaipur** — best two-player trading game on your shelf.
- **Mostly 3–4 and want build-and-trade?** Swap **Fluxx** for **Catan: On the Road**.
- **Want one more calm puzzle?** Swap **Fluxx** for **Ohanami** (drafting, but quieter than Sushi Go).

**Short answer:** Sushi Go!, Monopoly Deal, Rainbow, Point Salad, Fluxx — five decks, five moods, fits in one bag.

Want this baked into the draft as a "what I would pack" closing section?

From your shelf, **Jaipur** is the best portable two-player game.

**Why Jaipur wins:** It is built for two only — no awkward "the rules say use this variant at two players" fudge. Small box: cards and tokens, no board. About twenty minutes per round, best-of-three Seals so one bad round does not kill the night. The market teaches itself in a single pass: take from the middle or sell a set, camels off to the side, no direct stealing from each other's hands.

If you mean **the other four portable two-player games on your shelf** after **Jaipur**, here is how I would rank them:

### 2. Hanamikoji
Smallest footprint, sharpest game. Four turns each, ~fifteen minutes, mostly cards. Less trading than Jaipur — more “I split, you choose” tension.

### 3. Agent Avenue
Hanamikoji’s cousin: face-up/face-down split, chase on a track. Still small, still two-player only. More bluffing and misdirection than Hanamikoji.

### 4. Rainbow
Tiny box, works at two. Combo tricks, prizes recycle from the last round. Lighter than the three above — good when you want quick and done.

### 5. Ohanami
Quiet drafting puzzle at two. Bigger teach than Hanamikoji, but still card-only and portable. Better when you want to think, not negotiate.

**Just outside the five:** **Santorini** — excellent at two, but the blocks make it the least packable of your dedicated two-player games.
